dp-dft-bins.rationale: Rhythm alignment supports finite-record pattern matching; signed complex phase is explicitly outside clapping. The ordinary action now avoids an unrelated FIR-tap dictionary annotation. All transform facts stay visible.

dp-spectrum-scaling.rationale: Calibration steps, endpoint handling and physical units are more precise as direct procedures; an extra metaphor would obscure distinct amplitude and density normalisations.

dp-window-leakage.rationale: Soft edges support reduced distant leakage with central broadening, while the limitation explicitly rejects optical-focus equivalence and guaranteed separation. Window definitions and calibration remain visible.

dp-zero-padding.rationale: An enlarged existing photograph separates finer inspection from new observation; the limit correctly distinguishes exact denser transform evaluation from pixel interpolation.

dp-time-frequency.rationale: Overlapping exposures distinguish observation span from update spacing and retain within-frame blending. The stated limit keeps frequency discrimination separate from overlap.

dp-downsampling.rationale: The narrower doorway supports suppressing out-of-range content before reduction. The limit identifies sampled-frequency ambiguity rather than physical damage, and finite filter rejection.

dp-interpolation.rationale: Additional timetable slots preserve original times while reserving new positions. The limit requires bandwidth/filter assumptions and denies new high-frequency evidence.

dp-fast-convolution.rationale: Repeating calendar supports circular wrap; the limit requires numeric addition, sufficient padding and keeping the genuine filter tail.

dp-measurement-project.rationale: The lesson integrates an explicit experiment contract and separate predictions; another analogy would add no mechanism beyond the direct synthetic example.

corrections: Hann coherent-tone calibration described entire positive/negative lobes as non-overlapping. It now states the precise measured-bin condition: the mirrored tone contributes zero for exact correction or negligibly for approximation; the question carries the same assumption.

PSD integration could be mistaken for the exact unweighted finite-record mean square. It now explicitly identifies tapered periodogram integration as window-weighted, with independent squared-energy/Parseval checks.

Circular-convolution question supplied only a linear result without constraining the two FFT input lengths. It now names the four-sample input and three-tap FIR, excluding cropping ambiguity while preserving the answer and question id.
The project RMS card did not explicitly give units on its result-symbol definition. The R definition now names the acceleration unit already defined by u.

Measurement uncertainty interval linked to an existing CockroachDB timestamp definition. Added an independently NIST-sourced DSP measurement-uncertainty entry with precise aliases and coverage assumptions.
Time alignment linked to a speaker-driver-specific entry. Added a DSP sample-time-alignment definition covering causal delay, centred offline filtering and boundaries.

Orthogonality glossary referred to arbitrary distinct DFT-bin cosines, which could include identical positive/negative-frequency cosine partners. It now names distinct non-negative-frequency real cosine basis components; the source and RMS question link now point directly to the original-author orthogonality treatment.
gaps: PSD covers units, finite weighted integration and energy versus coherent-tone normalisation. Stochastic estimator variance, Welch averaging and equivalent-noise-bandwidth derivation remain outside this introductory scope.
The rate-reduction example establishes a particular default offline FIR result and interior transient exclusion; no general production stopband guarantee or streaming device deadline is claimed.
Overlap-add tail mechanics are tested across block sizes including FIR-longer-than-block and partial final blocks; production streaming optimisation and throughput benchmarking are outside scope.
The final project checks deterministic generated acceleration data. Physical calibration, clock accuracy, noise, drift and a full measurement-uncertainty budget require external measurement evidence.
